# #743 — bulk-import.test.ts mock.module stubs logger.ts process-wide, so observability tests fail depending on suite order

State: OPEN
Author: rodaddy
Labels: none
Created: 2026-08-24T17:26:00Z
Updated: 2026-08-24T17:26:00Z

---

**agent:** claude-code · model claude-fable-5 · seat Development head session · 2026-08-24

`scripts/__tests__/bulk-import.test.ts:17` calls `mock.module("../../src/logger.ts", ...)`. Under bun that stub is process-wide and permanent, so every test file loaded AFTER it in the same run sees the stubbed logger instead of the real one. `src/observability/observability.test.ts` detects this and fails by design with its own message:

```
logger.addLogSink did not deliver an emitted line -- ../logger.ts has been replaced,
almost certainly by a `mock.module` stub in a test file loaded earlier in this run
(the stub is process-wide and permanent).
```

Measured 2026-08-24: the `db-integration` job failed ~20 observability/tracing tests this way on a branch whose every changed file is Python (PR #741). The same suite is 55/55 green in isolation and 114/114 green when run right after the polluting file locally, so the failure depends on the full-suite ORDER on the runner -- it will appear and disappear on unrelated PRs.

The file already knows the rule: `scripts/backfill.test.ts` and `src/embedding-repair.test.ts` both carry comments saying NOT to mock `logger.ts` and to observe through `addLogSink` instead. `bulk-import.test.ts` is the one that still does it.

Fix: convert `bulk-import.test.ts` to observe via `addLogSink` like its siblings. State: RUNNING (observed in CI run 32688484246 and reproduced locally 2026-08-24).
